runbooks.text: RB-101: When checkout-api exhausts its database connection pool, compare active requests with pool utilization. The incident commander must approve changing pool limits. Do not restart the database automatically.

RB-102: Roll back checkout-api to the last known good application release only after incident-commander approval. Record the change ticket, confirm health checks and monitor error rate for ten minutes.
RB-103: A catalog cache miss spike calls for checking cache hit rate and upstream latency. This is not evidence of a checkout database connection leak.
RB-104: For payment-provider timeouts, check the provider status and the request idempotency key before retrying. Never store card numbers in incident notes.

alice_note: INC-2042: checkout-api exhausted its database connection pool after release 7.18. Initial pool cap was 20. Change CHG-884 is awaiting incident-commander approval. I prefer handovers with impact, evidence, and the next owner.
alice_update: INC-2042 update: the incident commander approved CHG-884. The checkout-api pool cap is now 40, replacing 20. The error rate is back below one percent. No database restart was performed.
bob_note: INC-3051: payroll-api has a private vendor escalation, case PAY-771. This note belongs only to the payroll responder. Do not include PAY-771 in checkout-api handovers.
